model: Daintree DCS lighting zone device (BACnet IP)
applies_to: Each lighting zone configured in Daintree Controls Software, exposed as a virtual BACnet device behind its WAC.
summary: Every lighting zone set up in DCS becomes a virtual BACnet IP device behind its Wireless Area Controller. The BMS can command the zone light level, change dimming limits, occupancy levels, delays, fade times and control strategy, and read people count, ambient light, occupancy and a zone fault code.
default_device_instance: Set in DCS (start/end virtual zone device ID range)
notes: AV 1 is commandable; the WAC's own scheduler, UI and REST overrides write it at priority 7, so a BMS must use priority 6 or higher to take control.
Writable but non-commandable points take whichever subsystem (scheduler, UI, BMS) wrote last.
AV 9 is not listed in the guide.
A non-zero Minimum Level does not stop the lights from being switched off.
All points support COV; device name is the zone name from DCS.

source.title: Daintree Controls Software (DCS) BACnet integration guide

integration.summary: Enable BACnet on the WAC in DCS and give the zone devices an instance range. Command AV 1 Light Level CMD at priority 6 or higher, pick the zone behaviour with MV 2 Control Strategy, and read occupancy, light level and the zone fault code.

minimum_points.name: Control Strategy
minimum_points.why: Zone mode: manual, auto on/off, timed on

minimum_points.name: Fault
minimum_points.why: Zone fault: 1 normal, 2 comm failure, 3 bad config

integration.enable: AV 1 Light Level CMD is commandable; internal DCS subsystems write at priority 7, so write at priority 6 or higher.
setup: Set in DCS (Configure > Gateway > BACnet settings): router device ID, network number, virtual network number, start/end virtual zone device IDs, NIC (wan or building), port (normally 47808).
Foreign device registration to a BBMD is available when the WAC is not on the BMS LAN.
The WAC routes BACnet IP to a virtual network; each zone is its own virtual device (B-ASC profile).
gotchas: Writing below priority 7 has no effect while the WAC scheduler or a manual override holds the zone.
Zone device instances come from the start/end range in DCS; leave room for zones added later.

points.name: Occupied Level
points.description: Level set on an occupied transition (default 100)

points.name: Unoccupied Level
points.description: Level set on an unoccupied transition (default 10)

points.name: Off Delay
points.description: Time from all sensors vacant to unoccupied (default 900)

points.name: On Transition Time
points.description: Fade time when lights turn on (default 0)

points.name: Off Transition Time
points.description: Fade time when lights turn off (default 0)

points.name: People Count
points.description: Sum of all people counters in the zone

points.name: Ambient Light Level
points.description: Average of the zone's photo sensors

points.name: Fault
points.states: 1=Normal operation, 2=Communication failure with associated device, 3=Invalid configuration

points.name: Control Strategy
points.states: 1=Manual control, 2=Auto On / Auto Off, 3=Manual On / Auto Off, 4=Auto On / Manual Off, 5=Timed On

points.name: Occupied
points.description: Occupied if any zone occupancy sensor reports occupied
